newsitem.title: FRANCE: BOBSLEIGH-LUEDERS PILOTS CANADA TO SECOND WIN.
newsitem.headline: BOBSLEIGH-LUEDERS PILOTS CANADA TO SECOND WIN.

text.p: Pierre Lueders piloted Canada to its second World Cup win in as many races with a victory in the two-man competition on Saturday.
Sitting fourth after the first run, Lueders and brakeman Dave MacEachern clocked the fastest second trip down the 1992 Olympic course finishing with an aggregate time of two minutes 00.50 seconds.

American Jim Herberich and brakeman Garrett Hines, had held a 15-hundredths of a second lead after the opening run, which was delayed almost seven hours as officials worked to clear the course from heavy snowfall.
But the Americans were unable to protect their advantage and for the second week in a row were forced to settle for second behind the Canadians with a time of 2:00.67.
The Italian team of Gunther Huber and Antonio Tartaglia were third in 2:00.76 followed by the Austrian sled of Hubert Schosser and Martin Schuetzenauer in fourth with 2:00.97.
